title: Submit Your Questions: Will Anyone Keep You Safe From AI?
gist: Promo for a WIRED subscriber-only livestream (Dec 2, noon ET) where Backchannel editors Sandra Upson, Steven Levy and Lauren Goode take questions on Big Tech and AI safety. The framing: the AI safety debate has lost focus, the industry has not adopted proposed curbs (training pause, data center moratorium), and critical infrastructure looks increasingly vulnerable.

insights.claim: WIRED's Backchannel team argues the AI safety conversation has lost focus: experts disagree on which catastrophe is most salient (existential risk, rogue-agent cyberattacks, societal collapse) but broadly agree society is in real trouble.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Lack of consensus on the primary AI risk makes regulatory outcomes harder to forecast, raising policy uncertainty for AI developers.
insights.quote: The AI safety conversation, as Lauren Goode put it, has lost the plot.
insights.locator: The AI safety conversation, as Lauren Goode

insights.claim: Proposals such as a pause in AI model training and a data center moratorium have been floated, but WIRED judges the AI industry has not made changes that reassure the public about AI safety.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Watch moratorium and training-pause proposals as tail risks to data center buildout and AI capex trajectories.
insights.quote: the industry hasn’t exactly made changes that are putting people at ease around AI safety
insights.locator: Though a pause in training models

insights.claim: WIRED's Backchannel editors frame critical infrastructure as becoming increasingly vulnerable as AI risks, including cyberattacks by rogue AI agents, grow.
insights.speaker: Sandra Upson
insights.so_what: Supports a demand thesis for critical-infrastructure cybersecurity and AI-agent security tooling.
insights.quote: critical infrastructure seems more and more vulnerable every day
